bib.title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

question: Can lightweight, synthetically trained LM judges plus a small human-labelled set give accurate, confidence-bounded rankings of RAG systems on context relevance, answer faithfulness and answer relevance?
hypothesis: Domain-tailored fine-tuned judges combined with prediction-powered inference rank RAG systems more accurately and with fewer annotations than few-shot prompted judges (RAGAS, GPT-3.5) or sampled human annotations.
contributions: ARES, the first automated RAG evaluation system to generate tailored LLM judges for each RAG component
Confidence intervals for RAG scores via prediction-powered inference (PPI)
Evaluation across KILT, SuperGLUE and AIS, with cross-domain tests

method.summary: ARES generates synthetic query-passage-answer triples with FLAN-T5 XXL from in-domain passages (positives, weak and strong negatives), fine-tunes three DeBERTa-v3-Large binary judges (context relevance, answer faithfulness, answer relevance), and scores RAG systems with PPI using a small human preference validation set to give 95% confidence intervals; systems are ranked by interval midpoints.
method.task: automatic evaluation of RAG systems (ranking and scoring)

datasets.name: KILT: NQ, HotpotQA, FEVER, WoW
datasets.split: validation subsets; nine mock-RAG splits per dataset with success rates 70.0% to 90.0% in 2.5-point steps
datasets.preprocessing: Negatives for mock systems sampled from same Wikipedia document or a random one

datasets.name: SuperGLUE: MultiRC, ReCoRD
datasets.preprocessing: open-domain versions: MultiRC retrieval over its seven domain passage sets; ReCoRD over news passages

datasets.name: AIS (WoW, CNN/DM)
datasets.source: Rashkin et al. 2022; ToTTo and QRECC excluded

datasets.name: XGLUE, CodeSearchNet, T-Rex
datasets.preprocessing: used only for failed cross-domain transfer tests

datasets.name: Synthetic query/answer training set
datasets.source: generated by FLAN-T5 XXL from in-domain passages; equal numbers of positives and negatives; filtered by top-1 retrieval of the source passage
datasets.preprocessing: weak negatives: random passages/answers; strong negatives: same-document passages or BM25 top-10, contradictory answers via few-shot FLAN-T5

models.name: DeBERTa-v3-Large
models.architecture: encoder with single linear binary classification head on [CLS]

other.use: synthetic query and answer generation, few-shot 5 examples

models.name: BM25, OpenAI ada embeddings, ColBERTv2; MPT-7b-Instruct, GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4; Facebook RAG (DPR + BART)

other.note: real RAG systems in Section 5.3, one passage retrieved each

training.objective: cross-entropy (binary classification per judge); described as contrastive learning framework
training.epochs: early stopping after three epochs with no improvement in loss on the human preference validation set
training.dropout: 0.1 on the [CLS] final hidden state input to the classifier
training.compute: several hours for fine-tuning (DeBERTa) and generation (FLAN-T5)

inference.prompting: GPT-3.5 judge: 8 few-shot examples; FLAN-T5 generation: 5 few-shot examples
inference.retrieval: FAISS IndexFlatL2 with text-embedding-ada-002 to filter synthetic queries that do not retrieve their source passage; real RAG systems retrieve 1 passage

parameters.human_preference_validation_set: approximately 150 datapoints minimum; 300 in main experiments; 200 for AIS

metrics.name: Kendall's tau
metrics.definition: (concordant pairs - discordant pairs) / total pairs between true and ARES ranking of mock RAG systems; above 0.9 considered successful

metrics.name: Judge prediction accuracy
metrics.definition: accuracy of predicted context/answer relevance on RAG evaluation sets

metrics.name: PPI range
metrics.definition: percentage points between lower and upper PPI confidence bound

baselines: sampled annotations (150 per mock system, 1,350 total)
eval.protocol: Mock RAG systems with known ground-truth rates; one Kendall's tau per dataset and criterion; no seeds or significance tests stated; answer correctness for real systems = output contains KILT answer

availability.code: stated publicly available on Github (URL not in text)

prompts.purpose: GPT-3.5 context relevance (NQ, HotpotQA, MultiRC, ReCoRD)
prompts.text: Given the following question and document, you must analyze the provided document and determine whether it is sufficient for answering the question. In your evaluation, you should consider the content of the document and how it relates to the provided question. Output your final verdict by strictly following this format: "[[Yes]]" if the document is sufficient and "[[No]]" if the document provided is not sufficient. Do not provide any additional explanation for your decision.

Given the following question, document, and answer, you must analyze the provided answer and determine whether it is faithful to the contents of the document. The answer must not offer new information beyond the context provided in the document. The answer also must not contradict information provided in the document. Output your final verdict by strictly following this format: "[[Yes]]" if the answer is faithful to the document and "[[No]]" if the answer is not faithful to the document. Do not provide any additional explanation for your decision.

Given the following question, document, and answer, you must analyze the provided answer and document before determining whether the answer is relevant for the provided question. In your evaluation, you should consider whether the answer addresses all aspects of the question and provides only correct information from the document for answering the question. Output your final verdict by strictly following this format: "[[Yes]]" if the answer is relevant for the given question and "[[No]]" if the answer is not relevant for the given question. Do not provide any additional explanation for your decision.

evidence.quote: linear warmup and linear decay (Howard and Ruder, 2018) with a 5e-6 learning rate and a 32 training batch size

results.claim: ARES judge beats RAGAS on context relevance accuracy (stated 59.9 points in Section 5.1, 59.3 in the introduction).
results.metric: context relevance accuracy gap vs RAGAS
results.setup: Mock RAG systems on KILT and SuperGLUE datasets, DeBERTa-v3-Large judge, 300-datapoint PPI set
results.quote: For context relevance, ARES with a fine-tuned LLM-judge is 59.9 percentage points higher than RAGAS
results.note: Introduction prints 59.3 percentage points for the same comparison

results.claim: ARES beats RAGAS on answer relevance accuracy.
results.metric: answer relevance accuracy gap vs RAGAS
results.quote: for answer relevance, our system is 14.4 percentage points higher than RAGAS

results.claim: ARES Kendall's tau is higher than RAGAS for context relevance on mock systems.
results.setup: average over six datasets, 300 PPI labels
results.quote: ARES averages a Kendall’s τ 0.065 higher for context relevance and 0.132 higher for answer relevance than RAGAS

results.claim: ARES with 300 annotations beats 1,350 sampled annotations while using fewer annotations.
results.metric: Kendall's tau gap vs sampled annotations
results.setup: mock RAG systems; sampled annotations = 150 per system for nine systems
results.quote: the Kendall’s τ for ARES is 0.08 higher on average, across both context and answer relevance, compared to sampled annotations, despite using 78% less annotations

results.claim: ARES is only slightly better than a few-shot GPT-3.5 judge with PPI.
results.metric: Kendall's tau gap vs GPT-3.5 judge
results.setup: mock RAG systems, averaged over context and answer relevance
results.quote: averaging a Kendall’s tau 0.06 higher over both context relevance and answer relevance

results.claim: 150 human annotations is the minimum for ARES; NQ context relevance tau is 0.44 at 100 labels and 0.72 at 150.
results.note: Table caption: below about 100-150 datapoints ARES cannot meaningfully distinguish systems

results.claim: On AIS, ARES predicts hallucination rates within 2.5 points using 200 annotations.
results.setup: AIS WoW (707 examples) and CNN/DM (510 examples)
results.quote: getting within 2.5 accuracy points of the correct scores
results.note: Table 2 judge accuracy 62.5% WoW and 84.0% CNN/DM

results.claim: On real RAG systems ARES averages tau 0.91 for context relevance and 0.97 for answer relevance.
results.setup: NQ, WoW, FEVER; BM25/ada/ColBERTv2 x MPT-7b/GPT-3.5/GPT-4 plus Facebook RAG; 1 passage retrieved
results.quote: averaging a Kendall’s tau of 0.91 for context relevance and 0.97 for answer relevance
results.note: answer relevance 0.97; Table 5 ARES row averages 0.91 for C.R. and 0.99 for A.R.

results.claim: PPI confidence intervals were narrow and covered ground truth over 95% of the time.
results.setup: real RAG systems, context relevance; 6.1 points for answer relevance
results.quote: the PPI confidence intervals were 7.4 points wide for context relevance and 6.1 points wide for answer relevance

results.claim: GPT-4 labels in place of human labels lower tau by 0.05 to 0.30 in most settings.
results.setup: 500 GPT-4 few-shot labels as PPI set, NQ/ReCoRD/MultiRC
results.quote: While GPT-4 generated labels decreased Kendall’s tau in most settings by 0.05 to 0.30

results.claim: Judges transfer poorly across language, text-to-code and extraction shifts.
results.setup: judge fine-tuned on NQ tested on XGLUE (0.33), CodeSearchNet (0.28), T-Rex (0.38)
results.quote: a LLM judge fine-tuned on NQ achieved a Kendall’s tau of 0.33 over both context relevance and answer relevance scoring for XGLUE

results.claim: Memory/compute for judge and generator is about 32GB GPU.
results.quote: required GPUs with about 32GB of memory to run

limits: Needs a human preference validation set of roughly 150-300 datapoints, possibly from domain experts (law, medicine, finance).
Needs GPUs of about 32GB; fine-tuning takes several hours.
All datasets are English; judges do not generalise across languages, text-to-code or extraction tasks (tau 0.28 to 0.38).
Main benchmarks use mock RAG systems built by sampling negatives, not real system outputs; answer faithfulness is not tested on KILT/SuperGLUE for lack of hallucination labels.
GPT-4 as a replacement for human labels was worse than humans.
Seeds, significance tests, dataset sizes for synthetic data and warmup are not stated.
Baseline judge is gpt-3.5-turbo-16k version 10/23 and RAGAS 0.0.18, now dated.

terms.definition: is the retrieved information pertinent to the test question
is the response generated by the language model properly grounded in the retrieved context
is the response also relevant to the question
a statistical method that provides tighter confidence intervals on a small set of annotated datapoints by leveraging predictions on a much larger set of non-annotated datapoints
